why: funes-tendrils.py walks git forks mechanically -- but the studio's losses have never been git-only. Work strands in Claude project shelves, chats, Drive, Zapier skills, and sibling GitHub repos too (the v48 Confluence trunk lived in Drive for weeks while the repo served v43; the governance lane sat 194 commits stranded; the CYL harvest doc exists precisely because chats are unreachable later). This registry names every lane, what a sweep of it looks for, and -- critically -- HOW each lane can be reached. A lane no machine can walk is declared LOUDLY, never silently implied clean. That is the belt's own blind-gate lesson (tick 5) applied to memory itself.

reach_kinds.mechanical-ci: walkable by a script in CI with no credentials beyond the repo -- funes-tendrils.py owns these
reach_kinds.session-connector: walkable ONLY from a live Claude session holding the connector (MCP: Drive, Zapier, GitHub, Gmail, Dropbox). CI cannot reach these. The session-close sweep in CLAUDE.md owns them.
reach_kinds.human-only: no machine path exists from anywhere. Mitigation is discipline, not tooling: KD! ledger entries at session close, harvest docs for anything a chat produced that matters, and the standing rule that the shelf/chats are a CACHE -- a deliverable that only exists in a chat is NOT done.

lanes.check: working tree, unpushed, unmerged/stranded branches, worktrees, staging dirs, orphan pages -- funes-tendrils.py walks all of it today
each spoke's default branch vs its own unmerged branches; belt mount still green; anything committed to a spoke that the hub's cross-lane-manifest should point at

TSP-named files modified more recently than their repo counterparts (the v48-trunk loss shape); anything new in the studio folders that has no repo pointer. Drive is an address book -- a real artifact found here is a loose end by definition.
the deploy-studio-file skill still targets GitHub Pages; no skill drifted to a dead lane or stale repo path

UNREACHABLE by machine from any surface. The shelf is a CACHE (settled 2026-08-03). Mitigation: session-close KD! entry names anything that landed only on the shelf; next session's open walks it by hand from COLD-START.md's four-file list.

lanes.lane: chats / cowork sessions (Claude and other-model accounts)
lanes.check: UNREACHABLE by machine, ever, from anywhere -- proven by CYL_Harvest's access-boundary finding (a fresh agent cannot mine prior chats; confident reporting on them would be fabrication). Mitigation: anything a chat produced that matters gets harvested into a repo doc BEFORE the chat closes (the harvest-doc pattern), and TSP_Ledger.md is the decision record chats defer to. A chat that closed without harvesting is a loss already taken, not a loose end a sweep can recover.
